reason: E3 directly demonstrates that phase-selective recrystallization in a eutectic HEA achieves ~35% uniform elongation and ~2 GPa true stress, supporting the core mechanism and predicted outcome. E1 and E2 confirm that dislocation pile-ups at semi-coherent boundaries lead to cracking and limit ductility, but they do not provide evidence for the recrystallization intervention itself. The premises are thus mostly supported by accurately represented evidence, with minor reliance on E1/E2 for background rather than the intervention.
premises: Dislocation pile-ups at semi-coherent phase boundaries cause microcracking and limit ductility in eutectic HEAs
Phase-selective recrystallization of the ductile FCC phase can dissolve dislocation networks and reduce pile-ups
A recrystallized soft phase embedded in a hard-phase skeleton eliminates weak boundaries and releases strain hardening capacity
The treatment improves strain distribution and work hardening, enhancing ductility while maintaining or increasing strength
The concept is applicable to duplex alloys with soft and hard phases
